Lovastatin, a structurally similar inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, binds to Ugt2b7, suggesting a shared mechanism of action. The presence of a lowest common ancestor (LCA) between Simvastatin and Lovastatin, both as HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, implies a common pathway in their pharmacological effects. This suggests that the inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase by Simvastatin may lead to increased levels of certain metabolites, which in turn could affect Ugt2b7 activity. The observed relationship between Simvastatin and Ugt2b7 is thus mediated through the shared inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase, with the downstream effect on Ugt2b7 possibly contributing to the pathophysiology of Peripheral Nerve Palsy. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Simvastatin and Ugt2b7, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
